```text
Cumulative rules as of Sprint 3 (2026-11). Graded per PR out of 20: implements ACs 6 · tests + Test Evidence 6 · what/why + Tech Debt + linked issue 3 · CI or manual verification 3 · rubric review + approval on latest commit 2.

**Why:** these are graded line by line, and missing sections cost points even when the code is right.
**How to apply:** run through this list whenever drafting a branch, commit, PR body, or review.

## Branch & commit

- One branch per issue, cut from an up-to-date `master` (the course site says `main`; this repo uses `master`). Names: `feat/issue-<n>-<slug>`, `fix/issue-<n>-<slug>`.
- Commit: conventional prefix + issue number, e.g. `feat: add PDF export for reports (#42)`. The repo's agent rules also require an `[AI]` prefix on commits and PR titles made by an agent, so `[AI] feat: … (#42)`.
- Never push to `master` (it's protected). After merging, switch to `master`, pull, and delete the branch locally and on GitHub.

## PR body (all required)

1. `Closes #<issue>` (course wording; upstream uses `Fixes #` — `Closes` is fine). Attach the PR to the `Sprint N` milestone.
2. **What changed and why**, in the student's own words.
3. **Tech Debt** section with both fields: **Introduced:** (shortcuts or compromises made here, and why) and **Encountered:** (pre-existing debt met, and how it was handled). Write "None." when there is none.
4. **Test Evidence** section (S3+, replaces "how it was tested"):
   | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
   - One row per AC from the issue (for bugs, use the Expected Behavior instead). If there's no product behavior change (CI-only, etc.), write N/A and explain.
   - Test(s): test name + file; manual checks are written `Manual: <steps> → <result>`; list both if an AC is covered both ways.
   - Level: `unit` / `integration` / `E2E` / `manual`.
   - Source: `AC` / `issue discussion` / `docs` / `upstream behavior` / `other (explain)`. **The current output of our own code is never a valid source.**
   - Plus: **Not tested automatically, and why** (manual rows only), and **AI-written tests**: list tests AI wrote or changed and how their expected values were verified ("None" if none).
5. CI result. If CI isn't running, list the commands run and their pass/fail/skip counts (`yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint`, the workspace test command).
6. New or updated tests for every behavior change.

- Upstream Definition of Done (docs/sprint0/standards.md) also expects `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint:fix`, and passing tests to be run, plus a release note in `upcoming-release-notes/` (use the writing-release-notes skill).
- **Conflict to raise with the user:** `.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md` says agents should leave the PR template unfilled, but the course grades the PR body. Draft the course sections for the user and ask how they want them placed, rather than silently following either rule.

## Review & merge

- No self-approval or self-merge. At least one teammate approves; **merge only if that approval is on the latest commit** (any push after approval needs a new approval).
- Request the review on GitHub and ping the reviewer on Zulip. Reviewers reply within 24h.
- The reviewer posts a **rubric comment during the first review pass**, before the author revises, scoring 1–10 with a 1–2 sentence note each: Correctness · Test coverage · Code quality · Documentation · AI transparency (evidence of human verification) · **Test evidence** (S3: does every AC have a test, are expected values justified, which tests did the reviewer run locally) · Overall (merge as-is?). "LGTM" or approval alone doesn't count.
- Everyone reviews at least once per sprint, and everyone must review every teammate at least once over the semester.
- Anything posted to GitHub by the agent starts with 🤖 (repo rule).
- The student must be able to explain every line. When implementing, explain the changes, rationale, and risks before they're accepted.
- Skipped tests and disabled checks need a linked issue and a reason in a code comment. The team may not introduce new test failures.

name: course-issue-requirements
description: 'Checklist for writing or reviewing GitHub issues/specs in the CSCI 435 team repo — feature/bug/task formats, ACs, design decisions, spec-review comment, scope labels'
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c234029d-15b4-4a34-81c4-d33c3beb84df
  modified: 2026-11-09T21:59:19.100Z
---

**Why:** specs are worth 20 pts per sprint and design decisions 5, graded individually and strictly.
**How to apply:** use these formats when drafting or reviewing any issue. Agents may not _create_ issues (a repo hook blocks it), so draft the title and body for the user to file. Editing and commenting on existing issues is allowed, with 🤖 as the first character.

## Spec written and reviewed BEFORE any code

Exact S3 wording (verified 2026-11-09): "Before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment on the issue itself… the author updates the spec." The site does NOT require the author to be the implementer, and does NOT bar the reviewer from implementing. "Owner" appears only for sub-issues of the instructor's feature ("each with its own owner, spec (D2), and scope"). D2 is individual, so spec credit likely goes to the issue's author: a student implementing someone else's spec needs their own authored specs elsewhere. Don't claim stricter role rules than this.

**Feature / enhancement** (user story must meet INVEST):

- User Story: "As a [user], I want [goal] so that [benefit]."
- User Scenario: a concrete walkthrough.
- Acceptance Criteria: numbered, **at least 3**, each testable with a clear pass/fail.
- Out of Scope
- Open Questions

**Bug:** Observed Behavior (OB) · Expected Behavior (EB) · numbered Steps to Reproduce (S2R) · Additional Info (screenshots, logs, stack traces).

**Task / hardening** (S3): Problem · Goal · Acceptance Criteria · other details.

**Scope justification (S3):** state small or medium, plus 1–2 sentences on the components touched and the expected size of the change. The instructor may reclassify inflated scope.

- Labels: `scope: small|medium|large|xl`, `type: feature|improvement|bug`.
- Sprint minimum per member: 2 medium issues (535 adds 1 small). Large/XL issues get split into sub-issues.

## Design decision (at least one non-trivial decision per issue)

In a `## Design` section of the issue body, an issue comment, or the PR description (cross-issue decisions go in `docs/sprintN/design.md`). Fields, one sentence each is enough:

- **Decision**
- **Alternatives considered**: **at least 2 concrete options** (strictly graded)
- **Rationale**
- **Consequences**: what becomes easier, and what becomes harder

## Spec review comment (S3, posted on the issue by a teammate)

Must state: whether each AC is clear and testable · which cases were considered and whether they're covered · whether the scope fits. "Looks good!" alone fails.

## Hardening issue evidence (S3, optional issue type)

- Bug fix: a test that fails before the fix and passes after.
- Flaky test: root cause + repeated runs before and after (~20 for unit, ~10 for E2E).
- CI fix: links to CI runs before and after.
- Baseline failures: pass/fail counts before and after, plus the cause of each failure group.
- Regenerating snapshots, reformatting, or silencing a check without fixing the cause counts as small at most.
- Sources: baseline failures, flaky tests, broken CI, PR Tech Debt fields, known bugs, the upstream tracker.

## Backlog / carryover

Unfinished issues from the previous sprint go first; any dropped one needs its reason documented on the issue (closed / invalidated / no longer relevant). Attach everything to the `Sprint N` milestone, with one assignee per issue.
```

````text
Before starting: record baseline test results at the `-csci435-s2` tag (needed for the D8 suite-health section), and try the mutation tool early.

## D6 Mutation testing (new)

- Tool: **StrykerJS with the Vitest runner** (Actual Budget). Hand-made mutations don't count.
- Pick one issue whose PR changes both source and tests; mutate **only the source files changed by that PR** (535: two issues).
- Add `"json"` to Stryker `reporters`. Commit `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and `-after.json`, plus the config and command. Reusing a teammate's config is fine if credited, but each student runs it themselves.
- Analyze every survivor (if more than 10, at least 10, starting with lines the PR changed): **equivalent** or **test gap**, and why.
- Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a gap survivor; it must show as killed in the "after" report. Scores quoted in the write-up must match the reports.
- Write-up `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<username>.md`: title `Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <title>`. Header fields: PR(s), Tool, Config (link + credit), Command, Reports (before/after links), Mutation score before% → after%. Surviving mutants table (Location file:line | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why). New or strengthened test (commit link, file › test name, which mutant it kills). Questions: (1) what survivors revealed about the tests; (2) whether any survivor exposed an assertion whose expected value wasn't based on the requirements; (3) AI use and what was verified or corrected, or N/A.
- Rubric: tool run on PR files with config, command, and reports committed 4 · survivors analyzed correctly 4 · a killing test, confirmed by re-run 4 · answers show understanding 3.
- Common problems: tests that already fail on unchanged code stop Stryker, so fix or exclude them; tests that run against `dist` never see the mutants; narrowing the test set can produce fake survivors. If blocked, ask teammates first, then the TA early (with the errors and the AI log).

Extra credit: an upstream PR accepted or under active review (+3 each); an upstream bug report confirmed by maintainers (+2 each).

**Why:** graded strictly. Summaries, paraphrased prompts, share links, screenshots, or output without its prompts get no credit, and an unlinked log counts as missing.
**How to apply:** whenever finishing work on an issue or PR, or writing a report's AI section, check the log is real and linked.

- Log **every** AI session on the project: code, debugging, review, understanding code, drafting issues, PRs, or docs, design talk. Unproductive sessions count too. "When in doubt, log it." (Course-admin questions don't need logging.)
- Path: `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<github-username>/` (this user: `tigerk9`). Never put logs in a teammate's folder.
- Name: `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md` (date = session start; lowercase hyphenated). Tool ids: `claude-code`, `claude-web`, `claude-desktop`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`, `copilot`, `chatgpt`, `other-<name>`. Example: `2026-11-08_claude-code_issue-96-implementation.md`.
- Formats: `.md` preferred, `.txt`/`.json` OK. Not `.html`/`.pdf`/`.docx`. Attachments go in a sibling folder named exactly like the log minus `.md`.
- Content: model + tool, the full prompt and response history, and (for agentic tools) every file edit and command. Must be captured at the time, never reconstructed afterwards.
- Capture: run sessions via `specstory run claude`. If one was started without it, `specstory sync` converts local history into `.specstory/history/`. Copy sprint files into the log folder and rename to the convention.
- SpecStory CLI (v2.17.0, checked 2026-11-10 via `--help`) is **not on PATH** in the dev container: plain `specstory` → "command not found". Binary: `/app/.specstory/bin/specstory` (repo copy: `.specstory/bin/specstory`). Run from the repo root. One session: `/app/.specstory/bin/specstory sync claude -s <session-uuid>`; `--print` writes to stdout, `--output-dir <dir>` changes the folder (default `./.specstory/history`), `--local-time-zone` for local timestamps (default UTC). The current Claude Code session's UUID is the last folder of the scratchpad path. Output is named `<UTC start>-<first words>.md`. Sync after the session's last reply (re-running updates the same file).
- Link: one comment per contributor per issue (implementer, reviewer, tester, and estimator each post their own). From S2 on it may go on the issue **or** the PR. It must link the **specific file**, not the folder and not a different issue. Edit the comment to add rows for later sessions. No AI used → still post the comment saying "No AI used" (and the folder must still exist).

Exact template (prefix with 🤖 when the agent posts it):

```
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation / Code review / Testing / Other

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-web | [link](ai-logs/sprint0/jsmith/2026-09-08_claude-web_understanding-issue-42.md) | Understanding the issue, locating relevant code |
| 2 | claude-code | [link](ai-logs/sprint0/jsmith/2026-09-09_claude-code_issue-42-implementation.md) | Implementing the fix and writing tests |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-08_claude-web_understanding-issue-42/](ai-logs/sprint0/jsmith/2026-09-08_claude-web_understanding-issue-42/)
```

Relative links in GitHub comments don't resolve, so use full blob URLs: `https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/blob/master/ai-logs/...`, and make sure the log is pushed or merged first so the link works.

End-of-sprint: `specstory sync` → export web chats → rename → move into the folder → push → confirm every issue/PR touched has a working AI Assistance comment.
````

```text
[AI] Show "(modified)" on eight report widgets with unsaved changes
bennettmatuszewski
master feat/issue-125-modified-label None
## Description

Adds a "(modified)" label to eight dashboard reports: Net Worth, Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar and Goal. The label appears next to the widget name whenever the report's current settings differ from the saved widget, matching the label Custom Reports already show. It disappears when the user changes the settings back, or after "Save widget" succeeds.

- Adds a shared change-check helper, `widgetModified.ts`, plus the label components `ModifiedLabel.tsx` and `ReportWidgetTitle.tsx`. Custom Reports now reuse the same label component.
- Each report gets a `*WidgetSettings.ts` module. What "Save widget" writes and what gets compared come from the same function, so the label only reacts to settings that are actually saved.
- AI tools (Claude Code) wrote a significant part of this change.

## Related issue(s)

Closes #125

## Testing

- New unit test files for the shared helper and each of the eight reports. Each report's test pins the list of settings "Save widget" writes, checks that changing each one shows the label, and checks that renaming does not.
- Page tests:
  - Goal (extended existing tests): the label appears, disappears after a successful save, stays after a failed save, doesn't appear for a rename alone, and never appears without a widget.
  - Net Worth (new `NetWorth.test.tsx`): walks through the issue's user scenario, plus the mobile header.
- Ran StrykerJS mutation testing on the nine new modules. 26 mutants survived the first run. After adding tests and removing code that had no effect, all nine modules score 100%, with every mutant killed by a test failure rather than a timeout.
- `yarn typecheck` and lint pass, and all report tests pass (15 files, 338 tests).
- Manual testing: checked by me and confirmed the behavior works locally

## Design decisions

- Show that changes are unsaved instead of blocking the user from leaving (the decision from #96). No changes to `App.tsx` or the router.
- Relative date ranges compare the range *setting*, not the dates it currently resolves to:
  - Sliding windows compare their length.
  - "All time" and named ranges such as "last month" or "year to date" compare only the mode.
  - Fixed ranges compare the exact dates.
  - So a widget saved as "last 6 months" won't show as modified when opened next month.
- The baseline is the saved widget fetched from the server. A successful save refreshes it, so the label disappears; a failed save doesn't, so the label stays.
- Each page waits until its saved settings have loaded before comparing, so the label doesn't flash during loading.
- On Calendar, the date filter added by clicking a day on the dashboard card counts as a change, because "Save widget" would save it.
- Renaming a Summary widget now saves only the name. Previously it also saved any unsaved "Show as" changes. This matches the other seven reports.
- "Save widget" stays enabled even when nothing has changed.
- Crossover adjusts the saved range when it opens: sliding windows move back a month, and ranges are fitted to the months that have data. That logic moved into `crossoverWidgetSettings.ts` so the page and the comparison share it.

## Scope:

- Included: the eight reports listed above, in both the desktop and mobile headers.
- Not included: Formula and the experimental reports (#126), Custom Reports (they already have the label), any prompt when leaving the page, and any change to `App.tsx` or the router.

## Tests:

- `widgetModified.test.ts`: time-range comparison (each mode, day vs month windows, defaults), filter defaults, and when `isWidgetModified` returns early.
- `*WidgetSettings.test.ts` (one per report):
  - Compared settings match saved settings, each setting's change is detected, the name is ignored, and empty settings match the defaults.
  - Report-specific cases: Spending's live comparisons, Summary's "Show as" content, and Crossover's range adjustment and category/account order.
- `GoalReport.test.tsx`, `NetWorth.test.tsx`: the page-level behaviour described above.

## Tech Debt

### Introduced:

- Eight small settings modules. Some defaults (for example Crossover's and Spending's) exist both in the page's setup code and in the comparison, so changing one means updating the other.
- Each page has a new `isRangeReady` state to wait for the saved date range to load.
- Only Goal and Net Worth have page-level tests; the other six reports have unit tests only.

### Existing:

- Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover and Calendar may stay stuck on the loading indicator when opened without a widget id (for example `/reports/cash-flow`). Not verified, and not fixed here.
- Crossover's sliding window drifts back a month each time it is saved and reopened.
- Calendar shows two error messages when a save fails.
- StrykerJS's Vitest runner doesn't work with this repo's Vitest 5 on Windows, so mutation testing had to use Stryker's command runner instead. The mutation-testing config isn't committed.

## Checklist

- [x] Release notes added (see link above)
- [x] No obvious regressions in affected areas
- [x] Self-review has been performed - I have read every line of this diff and can explain what each change does and why it is needed
```

```text
Show a "(modified)" label on the standard report widgets
None
['scope: medium']
### Summary

Add a shared way for a report to tell whether its current settings differ from the saved widget, and a "(modified)" label that matches the one Custom Reports use. Wire both into eight reports: Net Worth, Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar and Goal.

### User Story

As a user who edits Net Worth, Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar or Goal widgets, I want to see a "(modified)" label when my changes aren't saved so that I know to press **Save widget** before leaving.

### User Scenario

1. On the dashboard, the user opens a Net Worth widget.
2. They change the date range. "(modified)" appears next to the widget name.
3. They change the date range back to the saved value. The label disappears.
4. They add an account filter. The label reappears. They press **Save widget**, and the label disappears again.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. **Given** any of the eight reports opened from a widget, **when** the user changes a setting that **Save widget** would save, **then** "(modified)" appears next to the widget name.
2. **Given** a report showing "(modified)", **when** the user presses **Save widget** and the save succeeds, **then** the label disappears. If the save fails, the label stays.
3. **Given** a report showing "(modified)", **when** the user changes every setting back to its saved value, **then** the label disappears.
4. **Given** a report opened without a widget (for example `/reports/net-worth`, which has no **Save widget** button), **then** the label never appears.
5. **Given** the Goal report, **when** the user only renames the widget with the inline name editor (which saves right away), **then** the label does not appear.
6. Each of the eight reports has a unit test showing that the settings checked for changes are exactly the settings **Save widget** writes.

### Out of Scope

- The Formula and experimental reports (#126).
- Custom Reports, which already have this label.
- Any dialog or prompt when leaving the page, and any change to `App.tsx` or the router (see the Design section in #96).

### Open Questions

- Spending and Calendar can use relative date ranges such as "this month". Should a widget saved as "this month" show as modified next month, when the actual dates have moved? (Proposed: no. Compare the saved range setting, not the dates it resolves to.)
- Should **Save widget** be disabled when there are no changes? (Proposed: no. Leave it as it is, to keep this change small and unsurprising.)

### Scope

Medium: building the shared helper and label is a small part of the work. Most of it is reworking each of the eight reports so the same function builds both what **Save widget** saves and what gets compared, plus a test per report.

### Source

Split out of #96.

### Design

_Owner: record at least one non-trivial decision, with at least two alternatives, the rationale and the consequences. For example, how to detect changes: compare the current settings against the saved widget, or set a "touched" flag whenever a setting changes._
======
```

```text
+import React from 'react';
+import type { CSSProperties } from 'react';
+import { Trans } from 'react-i18next';
+
+import { Text } from '@actual-app/components/text';
+
+type ModifiedLabelProps = {
+  style?: CSSProperties;
+};
+
+/** Marks a report whose current settings differ from the saved ones. */
+export function ModifiedLabel({ style }: ModifiedLabelProps) {
+  return (
+    <Text style={style}>
+      <Trans>(modified)</Trans>
+    </Text>
+  );
+}

+import React from 'react';
+
+import { theme } from '@actual-app/components/theme';
+import { View } from '@actual-app/components/view';
+
+import { EditablePageHeaderTitle } from '#components/EditablePageHeaderTitle';
+
+import { ModifiedLabel } from './ModifiedLabel';
+
+type ReportWidgetTitleProps = {
+  title: string;
+  /** Shows the inline name editor when provided. */
+  onSave?: (newName: string) => void;
+  isModified: boolean;
+};
+
+/**
+ * The page title of a report opened from a dashboard widget, followed by a
+ * "(modified)" label while the report has unsaved settings.
+ */
+export function ReportWidgetTitle({
+  title,
+  onSave,
+  isModified,
+}: ReportWidgetTitleProps) {
+  return (
+    <View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
+      {onSave ? (
+        <EditablePageHeaderTitle title={title} onSave={onSave} />
+      ) : (
+        title
+      )}
+      {isModified && (
+        <ModifiedLabel
+          style={{ fontWeight: 400, color: theme.pageTextSubdued }}
+        />
+      )}
+    </View>
+  );
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+import * as monthUtils from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';
+import type {
+  RuleConditionEntity,
+  TimeFrame,
+} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
+import { isEqual } from 'es-toolkit';
+
+/**
+ * A time frame reduced to the setting the user chose, not the dates it
+ * currently resolves to. Relative ranges (for example a sliding window or
+ * "year to date") are re-resolved every time a report opens, so comparing
+ * their dates would flag a widget as modified just because time has passed.
+ */
+export type ComparableTimeFrame =
+  | { mode: 'static'; start: string; end: string }
+  | { mode: 'sliding-window'; shape: 'day' | 'month'; width: number }
+  | { mode: Exclude<TimeFrame['mode'], 'static' | 'sliding-window'> };
+
+export function toComparableTimeFrame(
+  timeFrame?: Partial<TimeFrame> | null,
+  defaultTimeFrame?: Partial<TimeFrame>,
+): ComparableTimeFrame {
+  // Mirrors the fallbacks in `calculateTimeRange` so a widget without a
+  // saved time frame compares equal to the range the report opens with.
+  const start =
+    timeFrame?.start ??
+    defaultTimeFrame?.start ??
+    monthUtils.subMonths(monthUtils.currentMonth(), 5);
+  const end =
+    timeFrame?.end ?? defaultTimeFrame?.end ?? monthUtils.currentMonth();
+  const mode = timeFrame?.mode ?? defaultTimeFrame?.mode ?? 'sliding-window';
+
+  if (mode === 'static') {
+    return { mode, start, end };
+  }
+
+  if (mode === 'sliding-window') {
+    if (
+      monthUtils.isValidYearMonthDay(start) &&
+      monthUtils.isValidYearMonthDay(end)
+    ) {
+      return {
+        mode,
+        shape: 'day',
+        width: Math.max(monthUtils.differenceInCalendarDays(end, start), 0),
+      };
+    }
+    return {
+      mode,
+      shape: 'month',
+      width: monthUtils.differenceInCalendarMonths(end, start),
+    };
+  }
+
+  return { mode };
+}
+
+export type ComparableConditions = {
+  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[];
+  conditionsOp: 'and' | 'or';
+};
+
+export function toComparableConditions(
+  conditions?: RuleConditionEntity[] | null,
+  conditionsOp?: 'and' | 'or' | null,
+): ComparableConditions {
+  // Same defaults as `useRuleConditionFilters`.
+  return {
+    conditions: conditions ?? [],
+    conditionsOp: conditionsOp ?? 'and',
+  };
+}
+
+// Drops keys whose value is `undefined`, the same way saving the widget
+// does, so `{ a: undefined }` and `{}` compare equal.
+function toSavedShape(value: unknown): unknown {
+  return value === undefined ? undefined : JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
+}
+
+type IsWidgetModifiedArgs<T> = {
+  /** False when the report was opened without a widget. */
+  hasWidget: boolean;
+  /** False until the report has finished loading its saved settings. */
+  isReady: boolean;
+  /** The saved widget settings, in comparable form. */
+  saved: T;
+  /** The settings "Save widget" would write now, in comparable form. */
+  current: T;
+};
+
+export function isWidgetModified<T>({
+  hasWidget,
+  isReady,
+  saved,
+  current,
+}: IsWidgetModifiedArgs<T>): boolean {
+  if (!hasWidget || !isReady) {
+    return false;
+  }
+  return !isEqual(toSavedShape(saved), toSavedShape(current));
+}

+// Vitest config for mutation testing the "(modified)" label (issue #125) with
+// StrykerJS. stryker.config.json runs it once per mutant.
+//
+// A standalone config rather than the full vite.config.mts: that config
+// copies public assets every time it loads, which fails when Stryker's
+// parallel workers load it at the same time. These unit tests only need
+// module resolution and the test-mode clock.
+import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
+
+export default defineConfig({
+  resolve: {
+    conditions: ['electron-renderer', 'module', 'browser', 'default'],
+    tsconfigPaths: true,
+  },
+  test: {
+    include: [
+      'src/components/reports/widgetModified.test.ts',
+      'src/components/reports/reports/*WidgetSettings.test.ts',
+    ],
+    environment: 'node',
+    globals: true,
+    setupFiles: ['./vitest.stryker.setup.ts'],
+  },
+});
```

```text
import type {
  NetWorthWidget,
  RuleConditionEntity,
  TimeFrame,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import {
  toComparableConditions,
  toComparableTimeFrame,
} from '#components/reports/widgetModified';

type NetWorthMeta = NonNullable<NetWorthWidget['meta']>;
type NetWorthInterval = NonNullable<NetWorthMeta['interval']>;
type NetWorthGraphMode = NonNullable<NetWorthMeta['mode']>;

export type NetWorthWidgetSettings = Required<
  Pick<
    NetWorthMeta,
    'conditions' | 'conditionsOp' | 'interval' | 'mode' | 'timeFrame'
  >
>;

export function getDefaultNetWorthInterval(
  mode: TimeFrame['mode'],
): NetWorthInterval {
  // A single month reads better week by week than as one monthly point.
  return mode === 'lastMonth' ? 'Weekly' : 'Monthly';
}

/** The settings "Save widget" writes for a Net Worth widget. */
export function buildNetWorthWidgetSettings({
  conditions,
  conditionsOp,
  interval,
  graphMode,
  start,
  end,
  mode,
}: {
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[];
  conditionsOp: 'and' | 'or';
  interval: NetWorthInterval;
  graphMode: NetWorthGraphMode;
  start: string;
  end: string;
  mode: TimeFrame['mode'];
}): NetWorthWidgetSettings {
  return {
    conditions,
    conditionsOp,
    interval,
    mode: graphMode,
    timeFrame: { start, end, mode },
  };
}

export function toComparableNetWorthSettings(
  meta: Partial<NetWorthMeta> | null | undefined,
) {
  const timeFrame = toComparableTimeFrame(meta?.timeFrame);
  return {
    ...toComparableConditions(meta?.conditions, meta?.conditionsOp),
    interval: meta?.interval ?? getDefaultNetWorthInterval(timeFrame.mode),
    mode: meta?.mode ?? 'trend',
    timeFrame,
  };
}

type SpendingMeta = NonNullable<SpendingWidget['meta']>;

export type SpendingWidgetSettings = Required<

    | 'conditionsOp'
    | 'compare'

    | 'isLive'

  >

/** The settings "Save" writes for a Monthly Spending widget. */
export function buildSpendingWidgetSettings({
  conditions,
  conditionsOp,
  compare,
  compareTo,
  averageRange,
  isLive,
  reportMode,
}: {
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[];
  conditionsOp: 'and' | 'or';
  compare: string;
  compareTo: string;
  averageRange: SpendingAverageRange;
  isLive: boolean;
  reportMode: SpendingMode;
}): SpendingWidgetSettings {
  return {
    conditions,
    conditionsOp,
    compare,
    compareTo,
    averageRange,
    isLive,
    mode: reportMode,
  };
}

export function toComparableSpendingSettings(
  meta: Partial<SpendingMeta> | null | undefined,
) {
  const isLive = meta?.isLive ?? true;
  const mode = meta?.mode ?? 'single-month';
  // Resolve the months the same way the report does when it opens, so a
  // widget without saved months compares equal to the defaults it shows.
  // This also ignores the second month of a live budget or average
  // comparison, which the report replaces with the first one.
  const [compare, compareTo] = calculateSpendingReportTimeRange(meta ?? {});
  return {
    ...toComparableConditions(meta?.conditions, meta?.conditionsOp),
    compare,
    compareTo,
    averageRange: normalizeSpendingAverageRange(meta?.averageRange),
    isLive,
    mode,
  };
}

import type {
  RuleConditionEntity,
  SummaryContent,
  SummaryWidget,
  TimeFrame,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import {
  toComparableConditions,
  toComparableTimeFrame,
} from '#components/reports/widgetModified';

type SummaryMeta = NonNullable<SummaryWidget['meta']>;

export type SummaryWidgetSettings = Required<
  Pick<SummaryMeta, 'conditions' | 'conditionsOp' | 'timeFrame' | 'content'>
>;

const DEFAULT_SUMMARY_CONTENT: SummaryContent = {
  type: 'sum',
  divisorAllTimeDateRange: false,
  divisorConditions: [],
  divisorConditionsOp: 'and',
} as SummaryContent;

/** Reads the saved "Show as" settings, falling back to a plain sum. */
export function parseSummaryContent(content?: string): SummaryContent {
  if (!content) {
    return DEFAULT_SUMMARY_CONTENT;
  }
  try {
    return JSON.parse(content);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to parse widget meta content:', error);
    return DEFAULT_SUMMARY_CONTENT;
  }
}

/** The settings "Save widget" writes for a Summary widget. */
export function buildSummaryWidgetSettings({
  conditions,
  conditionsOp,
  start,
  end,
  mode,
  content,
}: {
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[];
  conditionsOp: 'and' | 'or';
  start: string;
  end: string;
  mode: TimeFrame['mode'];
  content: SummaryContent;
}): SummaryWidgetSettings {
  return {
    conditions,
    conditionsOp,
    timeFrame: { start, end, mode },
    content: JSON.stringify(content),
  };
}

function toComparableSummaryContent(content?: string) {
  const parsed = parseSummaryContent(content);
  if (parsed.type !== 'percentage') {
    // The divisor settings only apply to percentages, and the report resets
    // the divisor filters when it opens with any other type.
    return { type: parsed.type ?? 'sum', fontSize: parsed.fontSize };
  }
  const divisor = toComparableConditions(
    parsed.divisorConditions,
    parsed.divisorConditionsOp,
  );
  return {
    type: parsed.type,
    fontSize: parsed.fontSize,
    divisorConditions: divisor.conditions,
    divisorConditionsOp: divisor.conditionsOp,
    divisorAllTimeDateRange: parsed.divisorAllTimeDateRange ?? false,
  };
}

export function toComparableSummarySettings(
  meta: Partial<SummaryMeta> | null | undefined,
) {
  return {
    ...toComparableConditions(meta?.conditions, meta?.conditionsOp),
    // Without a saved time frame the report shows all time.
    timeFrame: toComparableTimeFrame(meta?.timeFrame, { mode: 'full' }),
    content: toComparableSummaryContent(meta?.content),
  };
}

import * as monthUtils from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';
import type {
  AccountEntity,
  CategoryEntity,
  CrossoverWidget,
  TimeFrame,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { calculateTimeRange } from '#components/reports/reportRanges';
import { toComparableTimeFrame } from '#components/reports/widgetModified';

type CrossoverMeta = NonNullable<CrossoverWidget['meta']>;

export const defaultTimeFrame = {
  start: monthUtils.subMonths(monthUtils.currentMonth(), 120),
  end: monthUtils.subMonths(monthUtils.currentMonth(), 1),
  mode: 'full',
} satisfies TimeFrame;

/**
 * Fits a range to the months the report can show. The current month is never
 * included, so sliding windows end last month and "all time" spans every
 * month with data.
 */
export function adjustCrossoverRange(
  start: string,
  end: string,
  mode: TimeFrame['mode'],
  earliestMonth: string,
  latestMonth: string,
): [string, string] {
  const clampMonth = (month: string) => {
    if (monthUtils.isBefore(month, earliestMonth)) return earliestMonth;
    if (monthUtils.isAfter(month, latestMonth)) return latestMonth;
    return month;
  };

  let adjustedStart: string;
  let adjustedEnd: string;
  if (mode === 'sliding-window') {
    adjustedStart = clampMonth(monthUtils.subMonths(start, 1));
    adjustedEnd = clampMonth(monthUtils.subMonths(end, 1));
  } else if (mode === 'full') {
    adjustedStart = earliestMonth;
    adjustedEnd = latestMonth;
  } else {
    adjustedStart = clampMonth(start);
    adjustedEnd = clampMonth(end);
  }
  if (monthUtils.isBefore(adjustedEnd, adjustedStart)) {
    adjustedEnd = adjustedStart;
  }
  return [adjustedStart, adjustedEnd];
}

export type CrossoverRangeContext = {
  earliestMonth: string;
  latestMonth: string;
  latestTransaction: string;
};

/** The range the report shows for a saved time frame. */
export function resolveCrossoverTimeFrame(
  timeFrame: Partial<TimeFrame> | undefined,
  { earliestMonth, latestMonth, latestTransaction }: CrossoverRangeContext,
): TimeFrame {
  const [start, end, mode] = calculateTimeRange(
    timeFrame,
    defaultTimeFrame,
    latestTransaction,
  );
  const [adjustedStart, adjustedEnd] = adjustCrossoverRange(
    start,
    end,
    mode,
    earliestMonth,
    latestMonth,
  );
  return { start: adjustedStart, end: adjustedEnd, mode };
}

export type CrossoverWidgetSettings = Required<
  Pick<
    CrossoverMeta,
    | 'expenseCategoryIds'
    | 'incomeAccountIds'
    | 'safeWithdrawalRate'
    | 'estimatedReturn'
    | 'expectedContribution'
    | 'projectionType'
    | 'expenseAdjustmentFactor'
    | 'showHiddenCategories'
    | 'timeFrame'
  >
>;

/** The settings "Save widget" writes for a Crossover Point widget. */
export function buildCrossoverWidgetSettings({
  selectedExpenseCategories,
  selectedIncomeAccountIds,
  swr,
  useCustomGrowth,
  estimatedReturn,
  expectedContribution,
  projectionType,
  expenseAdjustmentFactor,
  showHiddenCategories,
  start,
  end,
  mode,
}: {
  selectedExpenseCategories: Array<Pick<CategoryEntity, 'id'>>;
  selectedIncomeAccountIds: string[];
  swr: number;
  useCustomGrowth: boolean;
  estimatedReturn: number | null;
  expectedContribution: number | null;
  projectionType: 'hampel' | 'median' | 'mean';
  expenseAdjustmentFactor: number;
  showHiddenCategories: boolean;
  start: string;
  end: string;
  mode: TimeFrame['mode'];
}): CrossoverWidgetSettings {
  return {
    expenseCategoryIds: selectedExpenseCategories.map(c => c.id),
    incomeAccountIds: selectedIncomeAccountIds,
    safeWithdrawalRate: swr,
    estimatedReturn: useCustomGrowth ? (estimatedReturn ?? 0) : null,
    expectedContribution: useCustomGrowth ? (expectedContribution ?? 0) : null,
    projectionType,
    expenseAdjustmentFactor,
    showHiddenCategories,
    timeFrame: { start, end, mode },
  };
}

export type CrossoverComparisonContext = {
  categories: Array<Pick<CategoryEntity, 'id' | 'is_income'>>;
  accounts: Array<Pick<AccountEntity, 'id'>>;
  /** Missing until the months with data have loaded. */
  range?: CrossoverRangeContext;
};

export function toComparableCrossoverSettings(
  meta: Partial<CrossoverMeta> | null | undefined,
  { categories, accounts, range }: CrossoverComparisonContext,
) {
  // Mirrors how the report reads the saved selections: no saved list means
  // everything, and categories that no longer exist are dropped. Reading
  // through the category list also puts both sides in the same order.
  const savedCategoryIds = meta?.expenseCategoryIds;
  const expenseCategoryIds =
    savedCategoryIds !== undefined
      ? categories.filter(c => savedCategoryIds.includes(c.id)).map(c => c.id)
      : categories.filter(c => !c.is_income).map(c => c.id);
  const incomeAccountIds = meta?.incomeAccountIds ?? accounts.map(a => a.id);

  return {
    expenseCategoryIds,
    incomeAccountIds: [...incomeAccountIds].sort(),
    safeWithdrawalRate: meta?.safeWithdrawalRate ?? 0.04,
    estimatedReturn: meta?.estimatedReturn ?? null,
    expectedContribution: meta?.expectedContribution ?? null,
    projectionType: meta?.projectionType ?? 'hampel',
    expenseAdjustmentFactor: meta?.expenseAdjustmentFactor ?? 1.0,
    showHiddenCategories: meta?.showHiddenCategories ?? false,
    timeFrame: toComparableTimeFrame(
      range
        ? resolveCrossoverTimeFrame(meta?.timeFrame, range)
        : meta?.timeFrame,
      defaultTimeFrame,
    ),
  };
}
```

```text
        : accounts.map(a => a.id);

    setSelectedExpenseCategories(initialExpenseCategories);
    setSelectedIncomeAccountIds(initialIncomeAccountIds);
    setSwr(widget?.meta?.safeWithdrawalRate ?? 0.04);

    const initialEstimatedReturn = widget?.meta?.estimatedReturn ?? null;
    const initialExpectedContribution =
      widget?.meta?.expectedContribution ?? null;
    const hasCustomGrowth =
      initialEstimatedReturn != null || initialExpectedContribution != null;

    setUseCustomGrowth(hasCustomGrowth);
    setEstimatedReturn(initialEstimatedReturn);
    setExpectedContribution(initialExpectedContribution);
    setProjectionType(widget?.meta?.projectionType ?? 'hampel');
    setExpenseAdjustmentFactor(widget?.meta?.expenseAdjustmentFactor ?? 1.0);
    setShowHiddenCategories(widget?.meta?.showHiddenCategories ?? false);

    setSelectionsInitialized(true);
  }, [
    selectionsInitialized,
    accounts,
    categories.list,
    isCategoriesLoading,
    widget?.meta,
  ]);

  useEffect(() => {
    async function run() {
      const earliestTransactionData = await send('get-earliest-transaction');

      const currentMonth = monthUtils.currentMonth();
      const previousMonth = monthUtils.subMonths(currentMonth, 1);

      // Set earliest transaction date
      const earliestDate = earliestTransactionData
        ? earliestTransactionData.date
        : monthUtils.firstDayOfMonth(previousMonth);
      setEarliestTransaction(earliestDate);

      // Set latest transaction date, ensuring it doesn't include current month
      const latestDate = monthUtils.lastDayOfMonth(previousMonth);
      setLatestTransaction(latestDate);

      const allMonths = monthUtils
        .rangeInclusive(earliestDate, latestDate)
        .map(month => ({
          name: month,
          pretty: monthUtils.format(month, 'MMMM yyyy', locale),
        }))
        .reverse();

      setAllMonths(allMonths);
    }
    void run();
  }, [locale]);
```

```text
function SpendingInternal({ widget }: SpendingInternalProps) {
  const locale = useLocale();
  const dispatch = useDispatch();
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const format = useFormat();
  const [budgetTypePref] = useSyncedPref('budgetType');
  const budgetType: 'envelope' | 'tracking' =
    budgetTypePref === 'tracking' ? 'tracking' : 'envelope';

  const {
    conditions,
    conditionsOp,
    onApply: onApplyFilter,
    onDelete: onDeleteFilter,
    onUpdate: onUpdateFilter,
    onConditionsOpChange,
  } = useRuleConditionFilters<RuleConditionEntity>(
    widget?.meta?.conditions,
    widget?.meta?.conditionsOp,
  );

  const emptyIntervals: { name: string; pretty: string }[] = [];
  const [allIntervals, setAllIntervals] = useState(emptyIntervals);

  const initialReportMode = widget?.meta?.mode ?? 'single-month';
  const [initialCompare, initialCompareTo] = calculateSpendingReportTimeRange(
    widget?.meta ?? {},
  );
  const [compare, setCompare] = useState(initialCompare);
  const [compareTo, setCompareTo] = useState(initialCompareTo);
  const [averageRange, setAverageRange] = useState(
    normalizeSpendingAverageRange(widget?.meta?.averageRange),
  );
  const [isLive, setIsLive] = useState(widget?.meta?.isLive ?? true);

  const [reportMode, setReportMode] = useState(initialReportMode);

  useEffect(() => {
    async function run() {
      const earliestTrans = await send('get-earliest-transaction');
      const latestTrans = await send('get-latest-transaction');

      const currentMonth = monthUtils.currentMonth();
      let earliestMonth = earliestTrans
        ? monthUtils.monthFromDate(d.parseISO(fromDateRepr(earliestTrans.date)))
        : currentMonth;
      const latestTransactionMonth = latestTrans
        ? monthUtils.monthFromDate(d.parseISO(fromDateRepr(latestTrans.date)))
        : currentMonth;

      const latestMonth =
        latestTransactionMonth > currentMonth
          ? latestTransactionMonth
          : currentMonth;

      // Make sure the month selects are at least populates with a
      // year's worth of months. We can undo this when we have fancier
      // date selects.
      const yearAgo = monthUtils.subMonths(latestMonth, 12);
      if (earliestMonth > yearAgo) {
        earliestMonth = yearAgo;
      }

      const allMonths = monthUtils
        .rangeInclusive(earliestMonth, latestMonth)
        .map(month => ({
          name: month,
          pretty: monthUtils.format(month, 'MMMM yyyy', locale),
        }))
        .reverse();

      setAllIntervals(allMonths);
    }
    void run();
  }, [locale]);

  const getGraphData = useMemo(
    () =>
      createSpendingSpreadsheet({
        conditions,
        conditionsOp,
        compare,
        compareTo,
        averageRange,
        budgetType,
      }),
    [conditions, conditionsOp, compare, compareTo, averageRange, budgetType],
  );

  const data = useReport('default', getGraphData);
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const { isNarrowWidth } = useResponsive();
```

```text
# Mutation testing: Issue #125 -- Show a "(modified)" label on the standard report widgets

**PR(s):** #163  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.0.0 (command runner; see [Setup notes](#setup-notes))  **Config:** [`packages/desktop-client/stryker.config.json`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/blob/87dc81a369ee959b8ac3c8825f97319fad854e67/packages/desktop-client/stryker.config.json) and [`vitest.stryker.config.mts`](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/blob/87dc81a369ee959b8ac3c8825f97319fad854e67/packages/desktop-client/vitest.stryker.config.mts), based on my loot-core setup from #91  **Command:** `cd packages/desktop-client && npx stryker run`
**Reports:** [before](reports/125-bennettmatuszewski-before.json) · [after](reports/125-bennettmatuszewski-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 88.62% → after 100.00%

| | Mutants | Killed | Timed out | Survived | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 246 | 210 | 8 | 28 | 88.62% |
| After | 237 | 237 | 0 | 0 | 100.00% |

Stryker counts timed-out mutants as detected, so the before score is (210 + 8) / 246. The after run has 9 fewer mutants because I deleted code that three of the survivors showed had no effect (see the Spending and Crossover rows below).

**What was mutated.** The PR's change-detection logic: `widgetModified.ts` (shared helper) and the eight `*WidgetSettings.ts` modules, one per report. The PR's edits to the report pages (`NetWorth.tsx`, `CashFlow.tsx`, ...) only wire those modules into the pages. Mutating whole page files would mutate thousands of lines the PR didn't touch, so I left them out.

## Setup notes

- **Vitest runner.** The required Vitest runner (`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.0.0) does not work with the Vitest 5.0.0 the repo moved to in the 2026-10-16 upstream merge. Its initial test run passes (118 tests), but no tests run for any mutant, so every mutant is reported as surviving (14% on my files). I checked this was not my config:
  - I ran my loot-core setup from #91 on `sort-categories.ts`, and the `asc`/`desc` mutants "survived" even though `sort-categories.test.ts` tests both directions.
  - When I switched a mutant on by hand (`__STRYKER_ACTIVE_MUTANT__=239`), the tests killed it.
- **Command runner instead.** I used Stryker's command runner, which starts Vitest once per mutant. It is still StrykerJS, but it is not the Vitest runner, so this deviation needs the TA's OK.
- **Standalone Vitest config.** `vitest.stryker.config.mts` runs only the 9 unit test files for these modules. The full `vite.config.mts` copies `public/` assets on every load, which fails with EPERM when Stryker's parallel workers load it at once.
- **Before report.** I deleted the report from my first run during clean-up. So `-before.json` is a second run of that same state: I temporarily undid the 3 code simplifications and removed the tests added after the first run. Its survivors match the first run's, plus three Crossover mutants at line 43 that the first run did not list as surviving.
- **Timeouts.** The before run's 8 timeouts (`widgetModified.ts` lines 37–45) were the machine being overloaded: four Vitest processes, each with several workers. One of them, 39:7 `&&`→`||`, survived in my first run. For the after run I added `--maxWorkers 1` to the Vitest command, and all mutants were killed without timeouts.

## Surviving mutants

All 28 survivors are in lines the PR added. "Gap" = a test was missing; "Equivalent" = no test can tell the mutant from the original.

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:14 | `defaultTimeFrame` → `{}` | Gap | The only test of a widget with no saved range resolved both sides through the same default, so changing the default changed both. Nothing checked that such a widget opens on "all time". |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:17 | `mode: 'full'` → `''` | Gap | Same gap as line 14. |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:34 | `isAfter(month, latestMonth)` → `false` | Gap | No test used a month after the last month with data, so clamping it was never checked. |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:43 | `mode === 'full'` → `false` | Gap | No test called `adjustCrossoverRange` with "all time", which should span every month with data. |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:43 | `'full'` → `''` | Gap | Same gap as the row above. |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:43 | `full` branch body → `{}` | Gap | Same gap as the row above. |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:50 | `isBefore(end, start)` → `false` | Gap | No test had an end month before the start month. |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:50 | fix-up body → `{}` | Gap | Same gap as the row above. |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:154 | `meta.expenseCategoryIds?.includes` → `.includes` | Equivalent | This sits inside `meta?.expenseCategoryIds !== undefined ? ...`, so the `?.` can never short-circuit. I removed it by reading the list into a local variable first. |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:160 | remove `.sort()` on expense category ids | Equivalent | Both sides are built with `categories.filter(...)`, so they are already in category-list order. I removed the sort. |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:161 | remove `.sort()` on income account ids | Gap | No test saved the same accounts in a different order, which the account selector can produce. |
| crossoverWidgetSettings.ts:171 | `meta?.timeFrame` → `meta.timeFrame` | Gap | No test compared a widget with no saved settings (`meta` null) before the months with data had loaded. That crashes with this mutant. |
| spendingWidgetSettings.ts:68 | condition → `false` (always keep `compareTo`) | Equivalent | `calculateSpendingReportTimeRange` already sets `compareTo` to `compare` for live budget/average comparisons, on both sides, so dropping it did nothing. I removed the branch. |
| spendingWidgetSettings.ts:68 | `isLive && mode !== ...` → `isLive \|\| mode !== ...` | Gap | This mutant also ignores the second month of a *live single-month* comparison, and no test changed that month while live. My first pass wrongly called all five line-68 mutants equivalent; this row and the next three are the correction. |
| spendingWidgetSettings.ts:68 | `mode !== 'single-month'` → `true` | Gap | Same gap as the row above. |
| spendingWidgetSettings.ts:68 | `!==` → `===` | Gap | Same gap as the row above. |
| spendingWidgetSettings.ts:68 | `'single-month'` → `''` | Gap | Same gap as the row above. |
| summaryWidgetSettings.ts:28 | `if (!content)` → `false` | Gap | Missing content then goes through `JSON.parse(undefined)`, which throws, so the catch still returns a sum but logs an error. No test checked that a widget with no saved content doesn't log one. |
| summaryWidgetSettings.ts:28 | early-return body → `{}` | Gap | Same gap as the row above. |
| summaryWidgetSettings.ts:33 | `catch` body → `{}` | Gap | Invalid saved JSON was never tested. With this mutant the function returns `undefined` and the caller crashes. |
| summaryWidgetSettings.ts:34 | log message → `''` | Gap | No test checked what is logged for invalid JSON. |
| summaryWidgetSettings.ts:65 | `parsed.type !== 'percentage'` → `false` | Gap | No test had divisor filters on a non-percentage total. The report resets those filters when it opens, so they must be ignored. |
| summaryWidgetSettings.ts:65 | if-body → `{}` | Gap | Same gap as the row above. |
| summaryWidgetSettings.ts:68 | non-percentage result → `{}` | Gap | No test switched between two non-percentage types, for example sum → average per month. |
| summaryWidgetSettings.ts:68 | `parsed.type ?? 'sum'` → `&&` | Gap | Content saved without a `type` was never tested; the page shows it as a sum. |
| summaryWidgetSettings.ts:68 | `'sum'` → `''` | Gap | Same gap as the row above. |
| summaryWidgetSettings.ts:79 | `divisorAllTimeDateRange ?? false` → `?? true` | Gap | A percentage saved without the "All time divisor" setting was never compared with one where it is off. |
| widgetModified.ts:77 | `value === undefined` → `false` | Gap | No test passed `undefined` to `isWidgetModified`. `JSON.parse(undefined)` throws. |

Timed out in the before run (counted as detected, listed for completeness): `widgetModified.ts` 37:34, 39:7 ×3, 41:7, 42:14, 44:16, 45:16. All eight are killed in the after run. 39:7 `&&`→`||` survived in my first run, a real gap: no test had a sliding window with one day-shaped and one month-shaped bound.

## New or strengthened test

Commit: [74854f42c](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/74854f42c84e9a4a97e62236ff148b5f278179ce) (the PR's commit, which includes the tests added after the first run) and [87dc81a36](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/commit/87dc81a369ee959b8ac3c8825f97319fad854e67) (Spending test and config) · Test: `summaryWidgetSettings.test.ts › Summary widget settings › ignores divisor filters when the total is not a percentage` · Kills: `summaryWidgetSettings.ts:65` (`parsed.type !== 'percentage'` → `false`), shown as Killed in the after report.

All tests added from this analysis, and the gaps they close:

| Test | Kills |
|---|---|
| `widgetModified.test.ts › toComparableTimeFrame › treats a window with only one day-shaped bound as month-shaped` | widgetModified.ts:39 |
| `widgetModified.test.ts › isWidgetModified › compares settings that are entirely missing` | widgetModified.ts:77 |
| `summaryWidgetSettings.test.ts › Summary widget settings › notices a switch between two kinds of totals` | summary:68 (`{}`) |
| `… › ignores divisor filters when the total is not a percentage` | summary:65 |
| `… › treats content without a type as a sum` | summary:68 (`&&`, `''`) |
| `… › treats a missing "All time divisor" setting as off` | summary:79 |
| `… › parseSummaryContent › falls back to a sum, without logging, when nothing is saved` | summary:28 |
| `… › parseSummaryContent › falls back to a sum and logs the error when the saved JSON is invalid` | summary:33, summary:34 |
| `crossoverWidgetSettings.test.ts › … more cases › ignores the order of the selected income accounts` | crossover:161 |
| `… › opens a widget without a saved range on all time` | crossover:14, crossover:17 |
| `… › can compare before the months with data have loaded` | crossover:171 |
| `… › adjustCrossoverRange › spans every month with data for all time` | crossover:43 |
| `… › adjustCrossoverRange › clamps a fixed range to the months with data` | crossover:34 |
| `… › adjustCrossoverRange › never ends a range before it starts` | crossover:50 |
| `spendingWidgetSettings.test.ts › … › notices a change to the second month of a live single-month comparison` | the line-68 gap (code since removed; I checked by putting the `\|\|` mutant back by hand: this test fails and the rest pass) |

## Questions

1. **What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**
   - **Main paths tested; defaults, fallbacks and edges not.** Each report's tests checked that changing every saved setting shows the label. They mostly missed what happens around those settings: values filled in when something isn't saved, fallbacks for bad data, and edge cases in range handling.
   - **Crossover** had the most survivors (12). Its range adjustment (`adjustCrossoverRange`) was only tested indirectly, through cases where both sides went through the same code. When the code under test runs on both sides of a comparison, a bug there cancels out, so the comparison tests could not see it.
   - **Summary** had no test for missing or invalid saved content. It also had none for "Show as" types other than percentage, which the report treats differently.
   - **Dead code.** Three survivors showed code that did nothing (a redundant branch, a redundant sort, an unreachable `?.`). I deleted that code instead of testing it.

2. **Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**
   - **Yes, two of the new tests.** Issue #125's requirements are about when the "(modified)" label shows. They say nothing about logging. The two `parseSummaryContent` tests check that a widget with no saved content logs nothing, and that invalid JSON logs `'Failed to parse widget meta content:'`. Those expected values come from the existing page code's behaviour (the log message was copied from `Summary.tsx`), not from the requirements. I kept them because they pin down the fallback, but they would break on a harmless change to the log wording.
```

```text
  interval: 'Monthly',

  timeFrame: { start: '2016-01', end: '2016-07', mode: 'static' },
};

function isModified(saved: Partial<Meta> | null, current: Partial<Meta>) {
  return isWidgetModified({
    hasWidget: true,
    isReady: true,
    saved: toComparableNetWorthSettings(saved),
    current: toComparableNetWorthSettings(current),
  });
}

    expect(isModified(SAVED_META, { ...UNCHANGED, [key]: value })).toBe(true);
  });

  it('ignores the name, which is saved separately', () => {
    expect(isModified({ ...SAVED_META, name: 'Renamed' }, UNCHANGED)).toBe(
      false,
    );
  });
```

```text
ummary
Add a shared way for a report to tell whether its current settings differ from the saved widget, and a "(modified)" label that matches the one Custom Reports use. Wire both into eight reports: Net Worth, Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar and Goal.

User Story
As a user who edits Net Worth, Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar or Goal widgets, I want to see a "(modified)" label when my changes aren't saved so that I know to press Save widget before leaving.

User Scenario
On the dashboard, the user opens a Net Worth widget.
They change the date range. "(modified)" appears next to the widget name.
They change the date range back to the saved value. The label disappears.
They add an account filter. The label reappears. They press Save widget, and the label disappears again.
Acceptance Criteria
Given any of the eight reports opened from a widget, when the user changes a setting that Save widget would save, then "(modified)" appears next to the widget name.
Given a report showing "(modified)", when the user presses Save widget and the save succeeds, then the label disappears. If the save fails, the label stays.
Given a report showing "(modified)", when the user changes every setting back to its saved value, then the label disappears.
Given a report opened without a widget (for example /reports/net-worth, which has no Save widget button), then the label never appears.
Given the Goal report, when the user only renames the widget with the inline name editor (which saves right away), then the label does not appear.
```

# Review of PR #163: "(modified)" label on eight report widgets

**The code is good to merge. The PR body and the issue are missing several items the course grades.** I found no correctness bugs.

## Test results (run on the PR head `e2aac2adc`)

I ran everything in a separate worktree, so your `feat/issue-153-update-vrt-workflow` branch wasn't touched. I've removed the worktree since.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| Report tests (`yarn workspace @actual-app/web run vitest --run src/components/reports`) | 41 files, 692 tests passed |
| `yarn test:debug` (full suite, no cache) | 9 of 9 workspace targets passed, 0 failed |
| `yarn typecheck` | passed |
| `yarn lint` | passed, formatting clean |
| Mutation reports | Scores match the write-up: 246 mutants at 88.62% before → 237 at 100% after |

I didn't re-run Stryker itself; I only recounted the committed report files.

## Code review

**What's solid:**
- **One function for both saving and comparing.** Each report's `build*WidgetSettings` builds what "Save widget" writes, and the same output feeds the comparison. "Save widget" now just spreads `...currentSettings` into the widget, so the label can't get out of step with what is saved. This also covers AC6.
- **Relative date ranges.** `toComparableTimeFrame` compares the range setting, not the dates it resolves to. Sliding windows compare their width, named ranges compare only the mode, and fixed ranges compare exact dates. That matches the issue's proposed answer to its open question.
- **No flash while loading.** Each page has an `isRangeReady` flag, so the label can't appear before the saved settings load. Spending skips it, which is correct: all its state is read on the first render.
- **Crossover date math.** This was the one place I expected a bug. The current range gets shifted back a month a second time during comparison. I traced it, and because `latestMonth` is always last month, both sides end up with the same width. No false "(modified)".
- **Refactoring.** Moving the duplicated Crossover clamping logic and Summary's JSON parsing into helpers is a real cleanup. The `defaultTimeFrame` moves keep the card files working.
- **Goal page tests cover AC2 fully:** the label disappears after a successful save, stays after a failed save, and doesn't appear for a rename alone.

**Minor code notes (none block merging):**
1. **`AgeOfMoney.tsx`:** the `useCallback` dependencies now include `currentSettings`, a new object on every render, so the memoization does nothing. Since the React Compiler is on, `useCallback` could just be removed.
2. **`summaryWidgetSettings.ts`:** `DEFAULT_SUMMARY_CONTENT` uses `as SummaryContent`. The repo prefers `satisfies`.
3. **Calendar:** opening a day from the dashboard card shows "(modified)" immediately. This is intended and documented, but it may surprise users, so it's worth calling out in the rubric.
4. **Page-level tests mock heavily.** For example, `NetWorth.test.tsx` replaces `Header` with a stub. That's fine for these tests, but the repo guide prefers fewer mocks. Six of the eight reports have unit tests only; the PR admits this in Tech Debt.
5. **Stryker isn't a dependency.** The config's `$schema` points into `node_modules/@stryker-mutator`, and the command is an unpinned `npx stryker run`. Pinning the version (or adding a devDependency) would make the run reproducible.

```text
## Minimum bar (every sprint)

No merged PRs, no sprint report, or no release → the whole team gets **0** for the sprint.

## Sprint report (`docs/sprintN/report.md`, or .pdf/.docx), team deliverable

Sections (S1 format, carried forward): Team (name, members + GitHub usernames, project, repo link) · Sprint overview (goals, what was actually delivered, honest scope changes) · Sprint backlog (milestone link + table: title, owner, points, scope, status) · Requirements & design (specs done before coding? surprises, key decisions) · Completed issues (table: issue, owner, PRs w/ link/author/reviewers/status, change summary) · Test strategy (test types; what couldn't be auto-tested and why) · AI tool usage (per member: tools, session count, folder link, 2–3 sentences on what worked or should change, patterns vs. previous sprint) · Release (tag + link) · Risks & retrospective · Next-sprint plan (ideas + carryovers).

- S2 added: Sprint 1 carryovers section, UML + check-in entries in the deliverables summary.
- S3 adds: **Suite health** (baseline table per relevant suite: command/CI workflow + passed/failed/skipped at the `-csci435-s2` tag AND at sprint end; failures grouped by cause with one linked issue per cause; no team-introduced failures; skipped tests and disabled checks need a linked issue + a reason in a code comment), links to every member's mutation-testing file, hardening issues + their sources, carryovers.
- Must **render on GitHub**: no escaped `\|` or `\[` in tables/links. Write fresh sections, don't copy the old report. Vague bullets earn nothing; be specific with links.

## Release (team)

- Never bump the version. Tag = the same base version + `-csci435-s<N>` (e.g. `v2.17.2-csci435-s3`). `git tag v<ver>-csci435-sN && git push origin v<ver>-csci435-sN`, then create a GitHub Release from it.
- Description summarizes features, fixes, improvements (S3: also hardening), not just the tag name. S3: create it **after the last Sprint 3 merge** so it matches final `master`.
- Look up the previous sprint's tag to get the base version (`git tag -l '*csci435*'`).

## Milestones

Each sprint needs a GitHub milestone named exactly `Sprint N` with all selected issues (S3: and code PRs) attached; each issue has exactly one assignee, and every member owns at least one.

## Mid-sprint check-in (individual)

`docs/sprintN/checkin/<username>.md`. S3 questions (~100 words each): what's implemented so far and what remains; one thing learned about testing in the project; one risk to finishing by Nov 19 and the plan for it. **Must link at least one code PR authored by the student that is open and ready for review, or merged, by Nov 12.**
```

```text
## Description

Adds a "(modified)" label to eight dashboard reports: Net Worth, Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar and Goal. The label appears next to the widget name whenever the report's current settings differ from the saved widget, matching the label Custom Reports already show. It disappears when the user changes the settings back, or after "Save widget" succeeds.

- Adds a shared change-check helper, `widgetModified.ts`, plus the label components `ModifiedLabel.tsx` and `ReportWidgetTitle.tsx`. Custom Reports now reuse the same label component.
- Each report gets a `*WidgetSettings.ts` module. What "Save widget" writes and what gets compared come from the same function, so the label only reacts to settings that are actually saved.
- Also adds the StrykerJS setup used for the D6 mutation testing (`packages/desktop-client/stryker.config.json`, `vitest.stryker.config.mts`, `vitest.stryker.setup.ts`) and the write-up in `docs/sprint3/mutation/125-bennettmatuszewski.md`.
- AI tools (Claude Code) wrote a significant part of this change. The log is linked in the AI Assistance comment below.

## Related issue(s)

Closes #125

## Testing

- New unit test files for the shared helper and each of the eight reports. Each report's test pins the list of settings "Save widget" writes, checks that changing each one shows the label, and checks that renaming does not.
- Page tests:
  - Goal (extended existing tests): the label appears, disappears after a successful save, stays after a failed save, doesn't appear for a rename alone, and never appears without a widget.
  - Net Worth (new `NetWorth.test.tsx`): walks through the issue's user scenario, plus the mobile header.
- Ran StrykerJS mutation testing on the nine new modules. 28 mutants survived the first run: 25 were missing tests and 3 were code that had no effect. After adding tests and deleting that code, all nine modules score 100% (88.62% → 100%), with every mutant killed by a test failure rather than a timeout. Details: `docs/sprint3/mutation/125-bennettmatuszewski.md`.

## Design decisions

### How to tell that a widget has unsaved changes

- **Chosen: compare the current settings with the saved widget.** Each report builds its "Save widget" settings with one function, and the label shows when the result differs from the saved `widget.meta` (after filling in the same defaults the page uses when it opens).
- **Alternative 1: a "touched" flag** set whenever the user changes any setting, and cleared on save.
  - Simpler to add to each page.
  - But changing a setting and then changing it back would still show the label, which fails AC3. Every setter on every page would also need to remember to set the flag.
- **Alternative 2: block leaving the page with a prompt** instead of showing a label.
  - Rejected in #96: it needs changes to `App.tsx` and the router, which is out of scope for this issue.
- **Rationale:** comparing with the saved widget is the only option that satisfies AC3. Building the saved and the compared settings from the same function also means a setting can't be saved without being compared, which AC6 tests.
- **Consequences:**
  - Each report needs a `*WidgetSettings.ts` module, and its comparison has to repeat the defaults the page uses when it opens. Changing one means updating the other (see Tech Debt).
  - Each page has to wait until its saved settings have loaded before comparing, so the label doesn't flash while loading (`isRangeReady`).

### How to compare relative date ranges

- **Chosen: compare the range setting**, not the dates it currently resolves to. Sliding windows compare their length, "All time" and named ranges ("last month", "year to date") compare only the mode, and fixed ranges compare the exact dates.
- **Alternative 1: compare the resolved start and end dates.** A widget saved as "last 6 months" would show as modified as soon as a new month starts, without the user changing anything.
- **Alternative 2: compare the saved `timeFrame` exactly as stored.** Pages save absolute dates even for sliding windows and re-resolve them when they open, so this has the same problem.
- **Rationale:** matches the proposed answer to the issue's first open question, and what "Save widget" would actually change.
- **Consequences:** `toComparableTimeFrame` has to know every range mode. It also absorbs Crossover's "move back one month" adjustment when it opens.

### Other decisions

- The baseline is the saved widget fetched from the server. A successful save refreshes it, so the label disappears; a failed save doesn't, so the label stays.
- On Calendar, the date filter added by clicking a day on the dashboard card counts as a change, because "Save widget" would save it.
- Renaming a Summary widget now saves only the name. Previously it also saved any unsaved "Show as" changes. This matches the other seven reports.
- "Save widget" stays enabled even when nothing has changed (issue's second open question).
- Crossover's range adjustment moved into `crossoverWidgetSettings.ts`, so the page and the comparison share it.

## Scope:

- Included: the eight reports listed above, in both the desktop and mobile headers.
- Not included: Formula and the experimental reports (#126), Custom Reports (they already have the label), any prompt when leaving the page, and any change to `App.tsx` or the router.

## Tests:

- `widgetModified.test.ts`: time-range comparison (each mode, day vs month windows, defaults), filter defaults, and when `isWidgetModified` returns early.
- `*WidgetSettings.test.ts` (one per report):
  - Compared settings match saved settings, each setting's change is detected, the name is ignored, and empty settings match the defaults.
  - Report-specific cases: Spending's live comparisons, Summary's "Show as" content, and Crossover's range adjustment and category/account order.
- `GoalReport.test.tsx`, `NetWorth.test.tsx`: the page-level behaviour described above.

## Tech Debt

### Introduced:

- Eight small settings modules. Some defaults (for example Crossover's and Spending's) exist both in the page's setup code and in the comparison, so changing one means updating the other.
- Each page has a new `isRangeReady` state to wait for the saved date range to load.
- Only Goal and Net Worth have page-level tests; the other six reports have unit tests only.

### Encountered:

- **Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover and Calendar may stay stuck on the loading indicator when opened without a widget id** (for example `/reports/cash-flow`). Not fixed: it's existing behaviour and outside this issue. The label is unaffected, because without a widget it never shows (AC4). Should get its own issue.
- **Crossover's sliding window drifts back a month each time it is saved and reopened.** Not fixed, since changing what Crossover saves is outside this issue. Handled for the label by comparing the window's length, so the drift doesn't show "(modified)". The adjustment now lives in one place (`crossoverWidgetSettings.ts`), which makes a later fix easier.
- **Calendar shows two error messages when a save fails.** Not fixed, outside this issue. The label behaves correctly: it stays after the failed save.
- **StrykerJS's Vitest runner (10.0.0) reports every mutant as surviving with this repo's Vitest 5.** Worked around by using Stryker's command runner, which starts Vitest once per mutant. The config is committed (`packages/desktop-client/stryker.config.json`, `vitest.stryker.config.mts`), and the evidence is in the mutation write-up.
- **On Windows, `yarn lint` and `knip` report hundreds of false failures locally,** because files are checked out with CRLF line endings. Handled by formatting only the changed files. CI on Linux isn't affected.
```

```text
## What have you implemented so far, and what remains?

So far I have implemented issue #125, which adds a "(modified)" label to eight dashboard reports (Net Worth, Cash Flow, Spending, Summary, Crossover, Age of Money, Calendar and Goal) whenever the report has settings that haven't been saved yet. Each report now builds what "Save widget" writes and what gets compared from the same function, so the label only reacts to settings that are actually saved. I added unit tests for all eight reports and page tests for Goal and Net Worth, and ran StrykerJS mutation testing, taking the score from 88.62% to 100%. What remains is getting the PR approved and merged, and following up on the reviewer's small code comments.

**Link:** [PR #163](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/163)

## What is one thing you learned about testing in your project?

One thing I have learned about testing is that code coverage doesn't mean your tests are correct. Using a mutation testing framework such as StrykerJS allows you to make sure your tests actually cover what they are supposed to and there are no gaps, something that a traditional code coverage report would not find. I also learned that these reports takea very long time to run. My tests took over an hour to run because there were many files change and stryker had to simulate many mutants which was quite time consuming.



## What is one risk to finishing your work by Nov 19, and what will you do about it?

The main risk is that PR #163 isn't merged in time. It's a large change across eight reports, so review takes a while, and any new code commit means the reviewer has to look at it again before approving. A second risk is that StrykerJS's Vitest runner doesn't work with our Vitest 5, so I used Stryker's command runner instead. To handle this, I have already updated the PR description with everything the reviewer asked for and will look into this to fixing in the future.

**Link:** [PR #163 review](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/163)
```

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.
